title: Antonelli and Mercedes 'faster than us' in US GP – Mekies
excerpt:
Red Bull's Laurent Mekies admits that Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes were "faster than us" in last weekend's United States Grand Prix, as Max Verstappen could only finish third.

Red Bull entered the event in Austin on the crest of a wave with Verstappen having taken back-to-back wins in Malaysia and Singapore.

The Dutchman started on the front row alongside polesitter Antonelli but failed to challenge the Mercedes driver at the start before Red Bull decided to utilise a two-stop strategy.

With Antonelli and Mercedes sticking to a one-stop, the young Italian was never seriously threatened as he won by 13 seconds from Charles Leclerc, the Ferrari driving having passed Verstappen in the closing stages.

"I think Kimi had more pace than us today. I don't think we can use any excuse of tyres or of strategy. I think Kimi was faster than us today. Fair play, and well done to him," said Team Principal Mekies.

"It's probably fair to say that one-stop and two-stop looks very close in terms of race times. We split our cars, as you have seen. I think Ferrari was on two stops, and I think McLaren was one-stop. So I think in race time, they were probably very, very close.

"It's probably fair to say that we normally enjoy a bit of an advantage compared to competition with the softer compounds, and today we have struggled to use that advantage.

"We have suffered some fairly high deg with Max on the two sets of soft compounds that we had – and that certainly didn't help materialising the second stop."

Red Bull's strategy played out with a new voice over the radio for Verstappen, as Tom Hart filled in the role for regular race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, who is set to move to McLaren.

How 'everything went wrong' for Red Bull in United States GP

Mekies believes Hart did a great job during a baptism of fire, with he and GP set to alternate the role until the end of the season.

"I think he did an excellent job, and you see me smiling because I certainly remember what it is to be on your first race as a race engineer," said Mekies.

"And he picked a fairly complicated race to do that, but that was not his choice! But joke aside, I think he really did an excellent job.

"First Qualifying, first race, he has managed to channel very well the work of the engineering teams behind him to Max. And of course the race was a complicated race, and we are probably a bit frustrated with the P3, which is the good news.

"But I really think he did an excellent job, and he was very well supported by GP as well in the background. You cannot recreate a relationship in no time. But I have every confidence that we are going to see him ramping up and building that relationship with Max."

One area of improvement that Mekies is keen to see is in regards to Red Bull's starts, with both Verstappen and team mate Isack Hadjar, who finished sixth, losing positions on the opening lap due to poor launches and sub-optimal battery deployment.

"As much as we have reduced the gap to competition, and you may remember how bad our starts were at the beginning of the year, we are still not the benchmark,” he said.

"And yes, the fact that the car in the meantime improved a lot and is fighting closer to the front makes that deficit even more painful now, because competition around us is very strong.

"On one side, I'm confident that we will continue to reduce the gap to the competition from now to the end of the year, because every race we learn, every race we come up with small ways to close the gap.

"On the other side, I equally know that we will not be the benchmark before the end of the season, that it will require some significant design and hardware changes, and that this is something that we will see only next year."

title: Vasseur admits to 'frustration' as 'pace was there' to win
excerpt:
The United States Grand Prix weekend was something of a mixed one for Ferrari, and in the end a solid second place was not quite enough for Charles Leclerc, who made it clear that he wanted more.

Not for the first time this year, the team looked good in practice, with Leclerc fastest on Friday, and Lewis Hamilton topping the times in FP3.

However things went awry when it mattered in Qualifying, with Leclerc having to settle for P4, and Hamilton for P5, albeit in a very tightly packed grid.

On race day the team went for soft tyres, and both men made progress at the start. As their chosen two-stop strategy unfolded Leclerc was able to charge up to runner-up spot behind Kimi Antonelli, passing Max Verstappen along the way, while Hamilton followed the Red Bull driver home in P4.

On the face of it, second was a decent result for Leclerc but after the flag he expressed some frustration, perhaps wondering what might have been had he started from higher than fourth – and potentially found a way to beat Antonelli.

“I don't know if you had all the radio, but very early in the race, Charles was targeting P1,” said Team Principal Fred Vasseur. “And when you do P2 and you target P1, you are not happy. But this I like as a feeling.

“Honestly, at the end of the weekend, I think it's a good week, a good result for us for the third or fourth race in a row, we are the team scoring the biggest amount of points.

“I think we are on the right way, but for sure, when you have this feeling that you are in a good shape on the weekend and you do P2, you can have also a bit of frustration. But the frustration sometimes is good.”

Vasseur was confident that the team had opted for the best strategy.

“Today I think that it was between one and two stops,” he said. “We had to be aggressive starting from P4, P5. It was a good call from us.

“Now when you start a bit behind, you start to have the dirty air, and you have to be a bit more aggressive. And without perhaps the Virtual Safety Car at the end, Lewis was perhaps able to come back on Max, I don't know. Probably yes.

“But overall, I think it's a good weekend in terms of pace, execution. Everything went well – except the last lap in Q3. It's true for us, but if you have a look on [Saturday], I think it was quite particular, that the two McLarens didn't improve, Russell didn't improve, the two Red Bulls didn't improve.

“I think what is true is that with the cars or the tyres, the window is very narrow, and as soon as you are a bit out, quickly you lose two or three tenths. And today in F1 [in] the top eight, two or three tenths can be a sixth position.

“It means that you can move from the super result to nowhere for gust of wind, or you slide a little bit too much in the out lap, or you have to slow down, as we had the case in Madrid, you have to slow down a little bit, don't stick to your pace in the out lap, or whatever, the impact is huge.”

Hamilton singles out his ‘biggest issue’ in United States GP

Vasseur insisted that the basic SF-26 package is a strong one, and the challenge is to optimise everything on a given weekend.

“Pace was good,” he said. “For sure the pace from the beginning when we put the car on track on Friday morning, to the last lap of the race, the pace was there.

"What we have to pay attention is that competitiveness is not just about the package; it's also the fact that sometimes set-up, tyre management, you are in the right spot, and you are doing a good weekend. And sometimes not.

“And if you have the package when you are not in the right spot, you can also have the feeling that it's not working.”

Finding that window, especially when it really matters in Q3, remains the big challenge.

“I think at least on this weekend, it was true for everybody,” said Vasseur. “Probably Kimi did a step also, because you can also imagine that he was not on the right spot before, and he put everything together for Q3.

“But I think the other seven cars, except Hadjar, probably the other six cars took a step back. The fastest lap of Charles was in Q2. For sure we didn't do the perfect job in Q3.

“That this is true for us, for everybody. But we have to put together all the parameters to try to have a better understanding of the situation. And I think all the teams we are improving step-by-step on this.

“But it's so marginal that sometimes a gust of wind, you are sliding a little bit, you overheat the tyres for details, sometimes you can be out of the spot. If you don't put everything together, you can move from P2 to P6.”

title: The single lap that cost Leclerc a shot at victory in Austin
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli drove the race of a champion one week too early.

Antonelli’s first victory since Madrid in September was as mature and as technically astute a drive as they come. He was clinical off the line, turning pole into the lead; he managed the gap to his pursuers during the opening laps; and then he slow-burned his tyres over two long stints to get the most out of the Pirelli rubber without risking runaway degradation.

It was the sort of performance that belied his inexperience in Formula 1 – and underlined why he has one hand and four fingers on the championship trophy, which he’ll have a second and better chance to take home in Mexico this weekend.

title: Wolff hails Antonelli’s ‘best race’ in Austin
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has claimed several memorable victories in 2026, but Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff believes his United States Grand Prix triumph was the best yet.

Antonelli didn’t quite put the World Championship beyond mathematical doubt, with Lewis Hamilton and George Russell remaining in contention. However, the Italian did all he could, taking pole position before delivering a dominant performance.

Victory was made all the sweeter by the fact that the team had struggled on Friday as they continued to explore the update package that was first seen in Malaysia, and which thus far has proved tricky to optimise.

However, by Qualifying Antonelli and his engineers had found the right window with his W17, and he never looked back.

“On Kimi's side obviously the main headline is that for me that’s the best race that he's delivered so far,” Wolff said on Sunday evening. “Getting off the start with the inferior tyre, and then controlling it at all times. The race of a champion – who isn't the champion yet – but exceptional.

“And so I think he's outperformed the car. Maybe it's a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in Qualifying yesterday, where on his last lap he could have been another tenth and a half or two up.”

Asked if he really thought that Austin outranked Antonelli’s charge from the back to victory at Monza, Wolff stuck to his guns.

“I've said that this is probably the best race I've seen, but my problem is that I don't remember past races!” he joked. “So now you saying Monza, it was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these Tifosi that were a little bit confused wearing red and hearing the Italian anthem, but with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium.

“I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year. Yeah, so both of them were pretty good. But the headline ‘this is the best’ we can keep!”

Reflecting on Antonelli’s form in 2026, Wolff also noted how relaxed the Italian remains despite the pressure surrounding the World Championship.

“I think maybe it was his benefit that the regulations were all new,” he said. “Last year he came in, and those cars existed for four years. The other drivers were used to it, and all new for everyone this year. And he just made it stick, with his mindset, with his easiness about approaching things.

“He's come to my office before getting ready, before getting dressed, and just sat down on that sofa and said, ‘I'm going to enjoy this one. And isn't it funny? I'm not thinking at all about the championship.’ And I said, ‘Well, exactly. Stick to that attitude. You have the best job in the world. Don't forget that.’ So he has also the right mindset.”

Wolff admitted that he still can’t quite comprehend the scale of the step Antonelli has made since last season.

“It's been 30 or more years that I've tried to understand the racing driver's brains, and I still don't know what has happened over the winter. His ability to process and deliver something that's outstanding, which we didn't see coming.

“But credit to him, credit to his engineers, to his environment, his family that he's delivered in that way.”

Naturally, Wolff is being cautious given that the title is not yet won. However when asked if he was proud of his own involvement in Kimi’s career – given that he is 99.9 percent of the way there – he provided an interesting insight.

“First of all, thank you, but I wasn't the one responsible for it,” he said. “It was teamwork. It was our junior team around Gwen [Lagrue] that discovered him when he was 11, and credit to that group that have developed him over the many years.

“I read an interview of Piero Ferrari last week where he said, ‘What a talent!’ He reminds him of Niki Lauda. And I'm thinking, people don't get that this is the work of nine years, the development of nine years, the hardship over nine years, the integration of the team, the working with the engineers, the 10 or more millions spent in the development of his career, of his ability, of his character, together with his parents, and it's just not that it landed like this.

“The many people that said last year after nine races without points he shouldn't be in a Mercedes. People that in other teams that said he shouldn't even be in Formula 1. The tears in Spa in in Parc Ferme, and all of that.

“Now it's extremely satisfying to see what he's able to deliver, how he's working with the team, with Bono, and yielding the results. But it wasn't an easy road. So yeah, I'm happy that like you say, it’s 99.9 percent.

“He still needs to finish the race in Mexico. So it's either going to be a big tequila party, or if it's not a tequila party, then it's going to be caipirinha the weekend afterwards…”

title: What the teams said – Race day in the United States
excerpt:
The drivers and teams report back on all the action from race day at the Circuit of The Americas for the United States Grand Prix.

Oct 26, 2026 1:20am UTC

Mercedes

Antonelli put in a masterclass in Austin, getting off the line brilliantly from pole despite being on the medium tyres. He built an advantage over Verstappen, the team holding their nerve when their rivals on a two-stop strategy began to pit. Antonelli remained on a one-stop, got his hard tyres working well after his trip through the pits and wound up winning by a comfortable margin to extend his lead in the championship and make it incredibly likely he will seal the title in Mexico City.

Russell had a harder afternoon, after picking up a time penalty on the very first lap for leaving the track and gaining an advantage when fighting Piastri. That dropped him behind the Australian when both stopped, and Russell just did not have the pace to get past the Mclaren on a day where his speed was nowhere near that of his team mate.

Kimi Antonelli, 1st

"What an incredible feeling. After Friday, I don't think any of us expected to be standing here with the win, so to turn the weekend around like this is really special. The car felt great today, and I was able to control the race, but it definitely wasn't easy. There was pressure throughout and I knew I couldn't afford to make a mistake. I just tried to stay calm, focus on each lap and execute the race.

"A huge thank you to everyone here at the track and back at Brackley and Brixworth. We kept working after a difficult Friday and never gave up. To repay all that work with a victory feels amazing. I'm very proud of what we achieved today."

George Russell, 8th

"It was another difficult day for me today. I just didn't have the pace and I'm unsure why that is. My first stint wasn't great, and I was struggling initially on the Medium tyre but after the pitstop my pace felt stronger and I felt I could make some progress. However, once I caught up with the McLaren of Piastri, I just couldn't overtake and ended up stuck behind him for the remaining laps of the race.

"The time penalty from the opening lap cost me a couple of places but overall, the pace just wasn't good enough today for me to be fighting at the front. The lack of performance is something me and the team will look at and work on over the next couple of days. Hopefully we can make some improvements ahead of next weekend in Mexico and come back stronger for the rest of the season."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"That was an exceptional drive from Kimi. He and the team didn't put a foot wrong all afternoon, showing strong pace throughout along with making all the right decisions strategically. What makes today particularly satisfying is where we came from on Friday. We didn't look like we had a car capable of winning this race, but the team kept working, made good decisions and turned the weekend around. That is a credit to everyone here in Austin and back in Brackley and Brixworth.

"For George, it was a more difficult afternoon, and the result doesn't reflect the pace we know he has. He was hindered by a five-second time penalty that dropped him behind the McLarens and then he got stuck behind Piastri. We will look at this weekend overall, understand what we could have done differently and work together to make sure he can have a stronger weekend in Mexico."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"Well done to Kimi and everyone in Brackley and Brixworth on the win. After Friday, a race victory simply didn't look achievable given our single-lap and long-run pace, so it's been a remarkable turnaround and a very satisfying result.

"For George, it was a frustrating afternoon. The penalty for going off track on the opening lap didn't help and, despite making a strong start to his second stint, he got stuck behind Piastri and couldn't find a way through.

"There were encouraging signs with the car pace, although since the update it does feel like the set-up window has become a little harder to hit. Operationally though, the team did a very good job. The strategy decisions weren't clear-cut, but we held our nerve, made the right call to stick with the one-stop, and the pit stops were solid.

"Most of all, Kimi should be incredibly pleased with his performances. It was a difficult Friday, but what he produced in qualifying, and the race today, was exceptional."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Race winner Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team lifts his trophy on the podium during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

Ferrari

Ferrari started well with both cars on the soft tyres, Leclerc picking off Verstappen and Hamilton passing Hadjar. Leclerc lost out to the Dutchman soon after, but once they pitted for some mediums, the car came even more alive. That enabled Leclerc to close back up to the leaders, and a late second stop for the hard tyre saw the Monegasque driver become the fastest man on the track. He closed up and got past Verstappen for P2, but did not have time to chase back to Antonelli.

As for Hamilton, he also two-stopped and easily picked off Norris towards the end. He looked on for a fun fight with Verstappen for the final podium place, until a late VSC neutralised that battle and saw the seven-time World Champion come home just one second off the rostrum.

Charles Leclerc, 2nd

"It was a fun race and I really enjoyed it, particularly the start and the battle with Max (Verstappen) on lap 1, and later on with Lando (Norris) and Max again. Our pace was quite strong, and our strategy was good, but it was not enough for the win today.

"We brought good upgrades to the car and have been going in a direction that I quite like. It makes me feel confident with the car so I'm optimistic. It's all about optimising what we have for the upcoming races, with the target of converting our progress to a win."

Lewis Hamilton, 4th

"Today was a strong team effort, with a solid strategy and great execution. I want to thank everyone here and back at the factory for their continued hard work which is helping us get closer. The balance in the race still wasn’t quite where I wanted it, but the pace was there and we were closing in the final stint. Without the VSC late on, I believe we’d have had a real shot at a double podium. That’s racing though, and there’s plenty to take from this weekend. The focus now is on starting strongly in Mexico and putting ourselves in the fight from the very first session."

Fred Vasseur, Team Principal

"It was a solid day for us: the pace was good and we were aggressive with our strategy. If there was something missing, it was in the final laps of Q3 yesterday. But I prefer to look at the positives from this race, starting with the fact that the pace was there until the very last lap today. I also think that, without the VSC towards the end, we could have come away with a double podium. We need to keep working and improving, especially in qualifying, to deliver an even better performance in Mexico next week. I want to thank the whole team, both here and in Maranello, for the solid job they have done which ensured a good weekend in terms of pure performance."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Race winner Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team and Second placed Charles Leclerc of Monaco and Scuderia Ferrari celebrate on the podium with Champagne during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains Lewis Hamilton driving the (44) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 and Charles Leclerc driving the (16) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 at the start during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Red Bull

Neither Red Bull got off the line well, both dropping positions through the first sequence of corners. Verstappen recovered back to P2, and went aggressive with an early stop for a second set of soft tyres. That guaranteed he was two-stopping, and when he came in again, he looked set to push for victory. But he could only make limited headway against Antonelli and instead found himself defending from Leclerc, who was on the same strategy. The Dutchman could not keep the Ferrari at bay, with car issues seemingly blighting his pace in the final stint.

He was moderately more happy than Hadjar though, who one-stopped after a solid effort to extend his opening stint on the softs. But the Frenchman’s pace faded and he wound up having a lonely end to the race between the two McLaren cars.

Max Verstappen, 3rd

"It wasn’t the strongest race for me, as there were a lot of things that didn’t work out and we seemed to experience different problems. The biggest question mark is why the tyres didn’t really work, while the harder compounds actually did really well, so that’s something to analyse. We struggled with engine consistency throughout the race, which we’ll need to work on, but it’s still a podium, so if you look at the beginning of the year and where we are now, we’ll take that. We’ve had quite a few podiums in a row, but at the same time, our target is always to be first, and we want to win more. It’s nice to see that we are now third in the Constructors’ Championship. The target for the rest of the year will be to keep that position. It’ll be tough, but we’ll keep working.”

Isack Hadjar, 6th

"It’s been a frustrating end to the weekend. We didn’t have a great start and lost two positions to both of the Ferraris, but from then on we settled into a rhythm and found really strong pace in the first stint. I felt good on the Soft tyre and I was lapping similar to the leaders, so the performance was there. I’ve been working so hard on the race pace, so it was good to see it in action. As the race went on, the tyre degradation was more manageable, so we moved onto a one-stop strategy. Unfortunately, we suffered a system issue in the pit lane which really compromised us for the rest of the race. We did a good job to keep P6 and bring a few points to the Team from what was an up-and-down weekend.”

Laurent Mekies, Team Principal

"It’s fair to say that, despite a 12th podium of the season with Max finishing third, we are leaving Austin not fully satisfied. We lost a bit of our edge today, and I don't think we had enough pace to fight with Kimi, who had a very strong race, so well done to him. Max’s car hit some debris around lap eight and picked up some damage. On top of that, we had a few issues that hurt the balance and, as a result, the pace dropped off, the degradation increased, and Max couldn't hang on to second place. It was a similar story for Isack, whose race was compromised by the start and then by a couple of problems during the race. Once again, the starts weren’t perfect, but the Team is working to make sure we have the tools to fix that in the future.

"A challenging Sunday, but we’ll take the podium knowing that we didn’t fully realize the potential of the car today, and we’ll take learnings from this weekend to come back stronger next week in Mexico. Despite all that, we have now moved up to third in the Constructors’ Championship, and Max is now only six points behind second place in the Drivers’ Championship.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Race winner Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team, Second placed Charles Leclerc of Monaco and Scuderia Ferrari and Third placed Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing celebrate in parc ferme during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Isack Hadjar of France driving the (6) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

McLaren

The two McLaren drivers held station off the line, Piastri making contact with Russell but unable to get past the Mercedes man. Whether that left him with car damage or not, he started to lose some time and the team opted to swap their drivers early on. Norris vindicated that decision by pulling away from his team mate, with both stopping early for the hard tyre to leave both the one and two-stop strategies in play.

In the end, both hung it out on a one-stop, Norris gambling from P2 but losing out to Leclerc, Verstappen and Hamilton while Piastri was able to defend from Russell and keep the Mercedes man at bay despite having much older tyres than his rival.

Lando Norris, 5th

“I feel I drove a strong race today and gave myself the best possible shot at a top result. Our pace on the Hard tyres was particularly strong, but to stay in contention and capitalise on potential Safety Car periods, I had to push the car well beyond its comfort zone. Ultimately, paying the price for that in the second stint meant fifth place was the absolute maximum we could achieve, and I am satisfied that we maximised our package under the circumstances.

“The reality remains that we are still lacking the outright pace needed to challenge higher up the grid. It was clear this weekend. Qualifying performance and car predictability remain our main priorities to address, but the team continues to do a fantastic job, and I am confident that if we resolve these key areas, we will secure strong results across the remaining races.”

Oscar Piastri, 7th

"P7 today. A tricky day out there. We just didn’t have the pace in the car, and we continued to struggle, as we have all weekend. The Hard compound was good, so we were able to extend to a one-stop strategy, having initially planned for a two-stopper, which helped us manage the track position in the second stint and keep George behind, which was positive. The strategy was strong, we had a solid start and pit stop, we just didn’t have the pace to be able to make up any places. When you find the window on these cars, there is some pace but finding that window is very tricky.

“Looking ahead to Mexico, we will review what we can from here to take into the weekend, where the combination of low grip and high altitude may prove tricky for us. But we’ll do what we can and keep pushing to add more performance to the car, so that we can maximise the lap time and pace.”

Andrea Stella, Team Principal

“A decent Sunday following a disappointing Saturday: that sums up the weekend in Austin. Today’s race showed that the MCL40 is still capable of fighting for the podium, but it’s clear that our position on the starting grid made that goal virtually unattainable. There is a shared sense of frustration across the whole team at not having fully exploited our potential during Qualifying, but it is up to us to try and do better.

“The team and the drivers worked very well, both in terms of strategic decisions and driving on the track, and the upgrades we brought here made a positive contribution: Lando showed excellent pace and Oscar drove a strong race, holding off Russell’s Mercedes for around thirty laps without ever giving him a chance to overtake. I was also pleased to see how our drivers worked together on the track, keeping in mind what the priority is, namely McLaren Mastercard’s best interests.

“Clearly, a fifth and a seventh place are not results we can be satisfied with, but we must accept it and work to improve. We want to end the season on a high and aim not only to fight for the podium but also for victory, with the aim of finishing the Championship in at least third place.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Oscar Piastri of Australia driving the (81) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes leads Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

Racing Bulls

Lawson started ninth and finished ninth, the Kiwi racer comfortably faster than his midfield rivals. He was also helped by those behind squabbling for position, giving him a chance to build a gap. He pitted just the once for the hard tyre, making those last for 31 laps. Lindblad was always in for a harder afternoon thanks to his grid penalty, but he did make progress up the field. He wound up two-stopping, and had one tight moment with Colapinto, but brought his car home in one piece.

Liam Lawson, 9th

"It's been a really positive weekend. The team have done a brilliant job with the upgrades they've brought to the car, so it feels great to be coming away with points. We executed the race very well and I've personally felt good in the car all weekend as it's in a strong place at the moment. We're still quite far behind the front runners, but to be at the top of the midfield and looking ahead should be seen as a positive. I'm looking forward to continuing this momentum and racing at some of the unique tracks we've got coming up. Big thanks to the team for all the hard work."

Arvid Lindblad, 12th

"It was a decent race. Unfortunately, I didn’t get the start I was hoping for and wasn’t able to make as much progress as I’d have liked on Lap 1. I struggled a little on the Softs during the first stint, but things improved on the Mediums, and we had a stronger second stint. I lost some time battling with Franco, which meant I had to push hard to try to catch Pierre, but ultimately, I wasn’t able to close the gap. We committed to a two-stop strategy today, and there are definitely some positives to take away from the race, but we’ll review everything with the team to understand whether there was anything we could have done better. Overall, though, I felt really good in the car, and it was an enjoyable race working my way through the field. It was one of those races where I was pretty much flat out from start to finish. I’m looking forward to getting back out there and racing in Mexico next week."

Alan Permane, Team Principal

"It’s been a very strong weekend for us. To have both cars in Q3 once again and then comfortably outperform our Championship rivals is a fantastic result. It was a textbook race from Liam; he controlled the gap to Pierre throughout and was driving well within himself and the car. Arvid picked up some damage to the left-hand side of his car relatively early on, which certainly compromised his performance. He did well to recover from 14th on the grid to finish 12th. It’s another valuable learning experience for him, particularly as it was his first time racing in Austin. Mexico presents another new challenge, but our aim is to carry the pace he showed on Saturday into the next weekend and deliver a clean race."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Liam Lawson of New Zealand driving the (30) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Arvid Lindblad of Great Britain driving the (41) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford makes a pitstop during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

Alpine

Gasly made contact with Bearman early on when his rival tried to dive down the inside, for which the Haas man picked up a penalty. Despite that, Gasly managed to climb back to P10 after dropping a place at the start and wound up finishing comfortably ahead of Hulkenberg to score a point for Alpine. Colapinto was not so lucky after starting towards the back thanks to that grid penalty. He wound up retiring the car with damage, his third DNF in the last four Grands Prix.

Pierre Gasly, 10th

“In the end, we started P10 and finished P10 and managed to score one point from today's race. Given the circumstances, I think that's good and that's all we could have achieved today. It was a pity about the incident with Ollie [Bearman] as it was quite a small contact but it brought quite significant damage to my car. Having seen my car after the race I was surprised to see the damage on the right-hand side floor with quite a lot of carbon fibre missing. Considering that, and our loss in performance, it was good to hang on to P10. We also had a slow pit-stop with a hardware issue, which the team is looking into to understand. I might have been able to compete with Liam [Lawson] and put some pressure on him for P9 but it was not the case today. All in all, I am pleased with a point and we go to Mexico City next ready to see what that weekend brings.”

Franco Colapinto, DNF

“It's not nice to be watching the end of the race from the sidelines again for a second race in a row, only this time due to picking up some damage. I was sandwiched between two cars going up the hill into Turn 1 and saw Pierre exiting the pits on my inside. Arvid [Lindblad] came around the outside and I was left with nowhere to go and unfortunately, we made contact. The whole floor and sidepod was broken which was enough not to continue to the end. We had opted to start on the Hards and try something different to the others, but it was always going to be tough to make much progress. The balance of the car felt good in clean air, but starting from the back we were impacted by running in traffic and dirty air. I'm now looking forward to going to Mexico City and hopefully turn our fortunes around.”

Flavio Briatore, Executive Advisor

“It wasn't really the weekend or the result we were hoping for. I think luck hasn't exactly been on our side recently. Both cars picked up damage during the race, with Franco's being significant enough to not finish the race. Given Pierre also lost downforce with floor damage following the incident with the Haas, he did well to score, get a point and only be one place behind the highest scoring Racing Bulls car. We head to Mexico City with the aim to improve our performance and score with both cars, which remains the objective at every race until the end of the season.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Oliver Bearman of Great Britain driving the (87) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari and Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes battle for track position during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Franco Colapinto of Argentina driving the (43) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Audi

Hulkenberg made a one-stop race work in Austin, starting on the softs and switching to the hards. But he did not have the pace to fight for the points, and was not helped by a poor start that saw him drop back through the field. Bortoleto was briefly investigated for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, but the stewards opted to take no further action. He pitted late on under the VSC for a fresh set of softs, and came home a couple of places behind his team mate.

Nico Hulkenberg, 11th

"Unfortunately, we lost some ground at the start when the car briefly went into anti-stall, which was a strange one because it happened a few metres after getting off the line rather than straight away. It felt and sounded a bit unusual, so we'll need to look into what happened and understand why. Obviously, losing those positions right at the start made the rest of the afternoon quite difficult.

"From there, I think we did what we could. Our pace was pretty similar to the cars around us, particularly the Racing Bulls, but once you're behind, it's difficult to recover. It's hard to say what might have been possible with a normal start, but the midfield remains incredibly close. We'll take what we can from this weekend and head to Mexico for another go."

Gabriel Bortoleto, 13th

“It was a good race overall; the car felt good and the pace was there. I overtook quite a few cars while keeping it clean, and I had a bit of fun being in the mix, trying my best and putting in some good laps. Obviously, it is always difficult to recover a lot of positions when starting from the back, but it’s good to leave Austin on a decent note. Hopefully, we can carry these positives into Mexico and have a better weekend next week.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director

“Both drivers delivered strong recovery drives today, although unfortunately we came away just outside the points. For Gabi, starting from the back row following the penalties for the changes we had to make, P13 was realistically the best result available. He drove a clean, very calculated race and made good progress through the field. Nico’s race was compromised at the start when the anti-stall kicked in, dropping him to P15. To recover to P11 and to close in on P10 was a superb effort. Ultimately, the result didn’t reflect the performance he delivered or what could have been possible with a clean start. We head to Mexico next week determined to turn that performance into points, and we’ll be back on the attack.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Eleventh placed Nico Hulkenberg of Germany and Audi F1 Team looks on in parc ferme during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Alexander Albon of Thailand driving the (23) Williams FW48 Mercedes and Gabriel Bortoleto of Brazil driving the (5) Audi F1 Team R26 battle for track position during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Haas

Bearman had a difficult afternoon in Austin, with contact early on damaging his car. He picked up a 10-second penalty for causing a collision with Gasly, as he tried to send it up the inside of the Frenchman. After serving that penalty, he wound up retiring the car with the damage too great to continue. That left Ocon to fly the flag for the team at their home race, and despite being let past his ailing team mate before Bearman called it a day, the Frenchman was unable to fight forward towards the points.

Oliver Bearman, DNF

“After the VSC, I managed to get a good launch and good battery level, because I caught the two cars in front of me very quickly. It made Pierre go defensive into Turn 12, and at Turn 13, I sent one up the inside, and to be honest, he saw me as he left space but to me, it didn’t feel enough. He gave space, but only half a car's worth, and I was committed, so we made a bit of contact – I picked up a huge amount of damage on my car, and I probably damaged his car as well.

"It was a shame as I felt like I was massively penalised anyway, as the damage ruined my race, and on top of that I picked up the penalty. In my view, it was a racing incident. I sent a move and felt entitled to more space than I got, I didn’t lose control, and I had to climb up the kerb to try and avoid contact. I don’t regret going for the move because at this stage in the season, if we don’t do anything special and get a bit lucky and be aggressive and go for it, we’re just not going to score points as we’re not always fast enough to score them on merit.”

Esteban Ocon, 14th

“We had a mega start, we always do, we’re leading the stats on that. Since the beginning of the year, we’ve always gained two or three places at the start, and we did that once again in COTA. I’m proud that we’ve worked so well on that, and the pit stop went well as well, but on the second stint, we struggled to keep the other cars behind. The problems that we faced throughout the weekend came back, as I still had front-locking, and I still had quite a lot of understeer in high-speed. These inconsistencies are something that we really need to work on and understand, and we need to make sure we get rid of them in Mexico. The positive is that we did reduce it a little bit with setup, but that’s the maximum we can do with the current parts.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“The race result was a shame, but I think there are lots of positives to take from this weekend. Both cars had great starts, and Ollie was fighting for P9 or P10, and without the damage he sustained, I think he had the speed to fight for that. We knew our race pace would be stronger than our quali pace. On Esteban’s side, he’s been fighting with front-locking issue, which got better, but towards the second half of the race, it came back and the pace wasn’t competitive. In terms of our operations, the fact that Ollie was happy from the get-go on lap 1, that’s exactly what we need. The fact that between Singapore and Austin, two very different circuits, we've unlocked performance – we’d like to build on that, and I hope we can fight hard in Mexico.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Oliver Bearman of Great Britain driving the (87) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari and Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes battle for track position during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Esteban Ocon of France driving the (31) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Aston Martin

Aston Martin saw both cars make it to the flag, but it was not a stress-free afternoon for the team. Alonso picked up very visible floor damage after colliding with Albon, bringing out an early VSC as the marshals were forced to go and collect some of his car from the track. He pitted for a new front wing which cost him some time, but out on track the Spaniard was happy to get involved and fight with the cars around him. Stroll came home just ahead, after opting for a two-stop strategy from a pit lane start.

Fernando Alonso, 16th

“We were quite competitive today and were having a strong race, but the damage to our car compromised everything for us. It felt like we were chasing down a potential points-scoring position as we were running in P12 with a damaged car. The damage was sustained from contact on lap one when Alex [Albon] hit us going into Turn 11. We carried on, but eventually had to pit for a new front wing and that dropped us down the order. We have some positives to take from this weekend despite the result today.”

Lance Stroll, 15th

“We had to make some changes to the car after Qualifying because of damage, so we started from the pit lane. Our pace was a bit more competitive today and I was racing [Alex] Albon for a lot of the race. There was a bit of overtaking too which was nice. We saw a big loss of load in the final laps though, so we need to go away and understand that.”

Adrian Newey, Team Principal

“Not the easiest race in Austin with both cars picking up issues and limiting performance. In Fernando’s case a front wing change was needed on lap 42, which stopped our efforts to deliver a one-stop strategy and dropped him out of contention. It seems the damage was a legacy of the contact with the Williams of [Alex] Albon on lap one. Before the pit stop, Fernando's pace was on a par with the cars ahead of him but we couldn't match their straight line speed which meant there was no option to overtake.

“Lance – having started from the pit lane – progressed up to P15 at the flag despite losing downforce at the rear of the car after his second pit stop. We need to look at the data to understand exactly what happened.

"Despite these issues, we will focus on the positives - both drivers were in the fight with decent race pace and extracted the most they could from the car today.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Alexander Albon of Thailand driving the (23) Williams FW48 Mercedes and Fernando Alonso of Spain driving the (14) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda battle for track position during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Lance Stroll of Canada and Aston Martin F1 Team looks on from the grid during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Williams

Both Williams drivers had action-packed afternoons in Texas, with Sainz squeezed towards the wall at the start by Lindblad, and emerging with what appeared to be some car damage. Albon also made contact off the line, his coming after he tangled with Alonso. The Spaniard came off worse, as those two then engaged in an entertaining multi-corner battle before trading places a few more times throughout the race for good measure.

Carlos Sainz, 18th

“We had another great start off the line but I got squeezed into the wall, had contact and picked up damage to my front wing. That compromised my first stint and I eventually had to pit for a new front wing, losing valuable time. From there it was a good recovery drive, with decent pace given the limitations of our car this week. Looking ahead to Mexico, it’s one track that we might be slightly stronger at, potentially with the ability to mix in with the midfield, but it’s going to take a lot to be back in the points.”

Alex Albon, 17th

“There were small positives to take from today. I got a good start and gained a few places on the first lap. Austin is a track where you can race and overtake, which I enjoyed, and there were a few battles with Fernando which we'll also review. We picked up some damage early on, and our long stint on the hards left us caught up in the blue flags. We're still lacking pace, and there's a lot of work to do. We'll need to find more for Mexico.”

James Vowles, Team Principal

“It's always disappointing to be unable to score points, but that's where the car pace was this weekend and both drivers got the most out of it that they could. Strong drive from Alex without any errors at all. With Carlos it was a good recovery and he executed his strategy nicely. It was good to see both of them racing cleanly towards the end – two incredible drivers, very respectful to one another. We move on to Mexico and beyond where we will try and eke out a few more milliseconds out of this car, but our main focus now is investing in 2027.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Carlos Sainz of Spain driving the (55) Williams FW48 Mercedes in the Pitlane during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Peter Fox/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Alexander Albon of Thailand driving the (23) Williams FW48 Mercedes on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Cadillac

Bottas did not see the flag in Austin, the Finn forced to park up late on with a power unit issue. That brought out a late Virtual Safety Car, which threatened to cause havoc with the pack before things settled down. As for Perez, he propped up the order on a day where Cadillac did not have the pace to compete. The tyre whisperer did manage to make his hard tyres last 32 laps though – although he did not take the honours, Piastri managing a 41-lap stint on the C2 rubber.

Sergio Perez, 19th

“Unfortunately, the weekend has been a bit challenging. Overall, I think there are positives we can take from it. We just need to keep working and learning from the experience. I think it’s really track-dependent, and during the race, I was surprised that we were a little closer than expected, so we just have to keep building on that.

“Now I’m really looking forward to Mexico. It’s always incredibly special to race in front of my home crowd, and this year will be even more meaningful as I celebrate my 300th Grand Prix. I’m excited to share that moment with the fans and hopefully give them something to cheer about. We’ll keep pushing and aim to have a stronger weekend.”

Valtteri Bottas, DNF

“The [suspected power unit] issue was really sudden and happened during braking into Turn 1. It started to sound bad and then I had the engine cutting in and out when trying to get on power. We don't know what the issue is yet. Up until then though, everything was going to plan. We decided to split the strategy across the cars - I started with the hard, Checo with the soft - and I think it was good to try. At certain times during the race it felt like we were actually a bit closer to the others on pace than what I thought we would be, so that was a positive we can take heading into the coming races.”

Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal

“Today presented a challenging race and we wanted to deliver a stronger result in front of our home fans. There were some encouraging signs in our race pace, with both drivers feeling closer to the competition than we had anticipated. We split the starting tyre strategies to give us options in the race and learn more about the compounds for the best possible team result.

”Unfortunately, Valtteri’s race ended with a suspected power unit issue, which we need to investigate fully. Checo brought the car home despite losing time in traffic. The team is operating much better at the track and I am happy with the progress, we just need a little bit more pace now to go fight with the teams ahead of us. With just a week until Mexico, our focus quickly shifts to preparing for another special weekend for the team, with Checo racing at home and celebrating his 300th Grand Prix.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Valtteri Bottas of Finland driving the (77) Cadillac F1 Team MAC-26 Ferrari on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Sergio Perez of Mexico driving the (11) Cadillac F1 Team MAC-26 Ferrari on track during the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 25, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Pirelli

Dario Marrafuschi, Pirelli Motorsport Director

“The United States Grand Prix proved a particularly fascinating race from a strategic perspective, with all three compounds used by the teams over the course of the event. The solutions we brought to Austin performed in line with the expectations that emerged over the previous days, with the Hard showing slightly better performance than anticipated. The degradation levels observed during the opening stint confirmed the projections made after the free practice sessions, making the one-stop strategy the most effective option, as demonstrated in the race, albeit by a very narrow margin.

"The two-stop strategies adopted by some teams were influenced primarily by Verstappen’s early pit stop, as he chased championship leader Antonelli, triggering a chain reaction in race management across the field. Drivers who were able to take advantage of clear air confirmed the competitiveness of the one-stop approach, maintaining a consistent pace all the way to the chequered flag. Tyre wear was relatively high and broadly uniform across the teams, without translating into any significant increase in performance degradation. From the perspective of tyre appearance, the overall picture was also remarkably consistent, with some more noticeable differences observed mainly on the Medium. The Hard rewarded the teams that incorporated it into their strategies, delivering consistent performance and a level of competitiveness that, for example, enabled Leclerc to pass Verstappen.”

title: All the key moments from the 2026 United States Grand Prix
excerpt:
The United States Grand Prix delivered another spectacular event that saw one of Kimi Antonelli's most dominant performances yet, with the Italian beating Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen to come tantalisingly close to his maiden title.

Plenty of other talking points emerged across the three days of action, from Red Bull's strategic and technical woes to George Russell's frustrating lack of pace relative to his team mate.

Here are all the key moments from the 2026 United States Grand Prix...

Antonelli on the brink of the championship after a dominant Austin triumph

Antonelli came into the weekend with his first chance of clinching a maiden world title and becoming the youngest ever F1 champion in the process. As it turned out, he was only two positions from doing just that on a weekend where he shone.

For the stars to align in Austin, the Italian needed to win Sunday’s race while also requiring Mercedes team mate Russell to finish ninth or lower, and for Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton to finish fifth or lower. Russell was eighth and Hamilton took fourth.

But Antonelli more than held up his end of the bargain as the young Italian came out on top in Qualifying and an excellent launch at lights out set him on his way to a dominant race victory – via a one-stop strategy that very much worked out for Mercedes. He now stands on the brink of title glory, needing only two points to seal the deal next weekend in Mexico City.

On the other side of the Silver Arrows garage, it was another weekend that left Russell with more questions than answers. While a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage on Oscar Piastri during the opening lap didn’t help matters, the Briton was at a loss to explain what happened to his pace as his team mate claimed a ninth career win.

Antonelli hoping to win title 'very soon' after 'perfect' US GP

Leclerc seals another podium as Hamilton closes in on P2 in the drivers’ standings

Ferrari went into the weekend surrounded by plenty of promise, helped in part by upgrades they were introducing. A practice clean sweep for the Scuderia – two for Leclerc and one for Hamilton – also helped boost the expectation.

Their rivals went on to lift their game over the weekend but – come race day – Ferrari mostly nailed things on the track as Leclerc lifted himself from a P4 starting position to second place. That’s his second consecutive runner-up position.

Hamilton, meanwhile, highlighted balance issues as his “biggest issue” in the race, but his fourth place result was still a successful outing and gives Ferrari plenty of optimism that they can be in the fight for the remaining races this season.

What’s more, the seven-time World Champion is now just a point behind Russell in the drivers’ standings – meaning his former Mercedes team mate is very much looking over his shoulder as he bids to keep hold of second place from now until the 2026 season comes to a close.

What happened to Red Bull’s pace?

Verstappen and Isack Hadjar both got off the line badly in Austin, the latter blaming a clutch “over-delivery” that has plagued him more than once this year. Both initially recovered in the first stint to look right in the mix for the win, especially when it transpired the team had split strategies to try and take the fight to Mercedes.

Verstappen went for an aggressive two-stop, having saved extra sets of soft tyres in Qualifying for the race. But that compound did not work as hoped, and he found himself with too much to do in his final stint on the mediums.

The Dutchman’s pace started to tail off too, something he later blamed on inconsistencies with the power unit. As such, not only could he not catch back up to the Mercedes of Antonelli to fight for the win, but he lost out to a recovering Leclerc and came home a slightly fortuitous third, helped by a late VSC that neutralised Hamilton’s charge behind.

As for Hadjar, he wound up losing out to Lando Norris despite both being on the same one-stop strategy. Considering how well he went in the opening stint, where the Frenchman got his soft tyres to sing lap after lap, sixth was a dispiriting ending and he admitted afterwards that the issues with his car were starting to “p***" him off.

How 'everything went wrong' for Red Bull in United States GP

A disappointing afternoon for McLaren

Norris and Piastri were clearly deflated with the lack of performance of their McLaren machines at the United States Grand Prix, with the reigning World Champion conceding that the team were “just not quick enough” in Austin.

Norris started on the fourth row in P7 alongside his Australian team mate in P8, with the pair struggling to match the pace of rivals Mercedes, Red Bull and Ferrari around the Circuit of The Americas.

In the latter stages of the race, Norris found himself second behind Antonelli but, on fading tyres, had a battle on his hands with Verstappen and Leclerc behind him before later dropping back and finding himself behind Hamilton to finish fifth.

It is now the fourth straight race without a podium for Norris, while Piastri’s disappointing 2026 campaign continued with a seventh-place finish – just over 1.6 second ahead of Russell.

“I think we achieved the best we could,” admitted Norris. “It was clear we didn’t have the pace of the others, but we gave it a good try.

“We had a good strategy and through everything, we gave ourselves the most opportunities so I’m happy, but we’re just not quick enough.”

The result leaves McLaren joint-third in the Constructors’ Championship alongside the improving Red Bulls, with the task ahead extremely clear in Norris’ opinion.

“We know exactly what we’ve got," he said. "But we’ve just got to improve it [the package] and at the minute, we’ve certainly made some improvements but it's nothing at the level it needs to be.”

A worthy champion in F1 ACADEMY

Alisha Palmowski took the F1 ACADEMY title in fine style in Austin, winning the crown with a round to spare. The British racer arrived in Texas with a commanding lead in the standings, so it was no surprise to see her take the title, the 20-year-old sealing it in the Reverse Grid Race with a superb drive from eighth on the grid to second at the flag.

She had already won the Opening Race in Austin from pole to extend her championship lead, before her P2 in the second race was enough to seal the title. Palmowski failed to finish the Feature Race, but that did not matter after such a stellar start to her weekend.

Palmowski is supported by Red Bull and has taken victory five times in her championship year, winning at least once at every round bar the opening weekend in China. The Campos Racing driver has 172 points and counting, with a dominant margin to Nina Gademan in second on 119 points.

F1 ACADEMY is heading to Las Vegas to round out the season, with Palmowski set for an effective victory lap down the Vegas Strip.

title: Hamilton singles out his ‘biggest issue’ in US GP
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has highlighted the “biggest issue” he had in the United States Grand Prix as he came home in fourth, while team mate Charles Leclerc claimed a second podium result in a row.

Much had been made of Ferrari’s promise this weekend in Austin, with the Scuderia bringing upgrades to the Circuit of The Americas, and the anticipation continued to build as both Leclerc and Hamilton topped Friday and Saturday’s practice sessions respectively.

However, come Qualifying their rivals had raised their game with the pair starting Sunday’s race in fourth and fifth behind the two Red Bulls, while Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli sealed an impressive pole position.

As the lights went out to kick off the Grand Prix, Antonelli’s launch was enough to see him set off on his way towards a dominant victory via a one-stop strategy. Meanwhile the Ferrari pair were instantly in on the action as they usurped Isack Hadjar before both challenged Max Verstappen, Leclerc eventually finding his way past before the Dutchman retook second place.

As the race went on – with both Ferrari and Red Bull committed to two-stop strategies – Leclerc eventually fought back and passed Verstappen for second on the road late on, while Hamilton missed out on the podium with fourth. However, the seven-time World Champion cited balance issues as he fought to try and get the best out of his car.

“Yeah, I mean, I didn't have a new tyre to start on, so it put me a bit on the back foot compared to the cars ahead of me,” he said after the race. “So, I had a little bit more deg in that first stint than they did.

“A new tyre to a used tyre is about two seconds of race pace so I lost that in the first stint. But just balance was my biggest issue – balance was off. But I think the team did a great job in the stops and the strategy.”

Despite the issues he faced in the Grand Prix, Hamilton acknowledged that he was encouraged for the next races to come, though he did concede he had work to do in order to nail the car’s set-up earlier.

“I think Charles obviously did a great job this weekend for us to get… it's good for points to be ahead of McLaren so we can keep second in the Constructors’ Championship,” he continued.

“I've really got to try to extract more from this car in the next couple of races. I do believe I could be quicker if we could just get the set-up right.

"It wasn't far off, well it was at the beginning of the stint, and I just need to look into how we get to that conclusion and how I end up in that situation because it's happened a few times, like in Silverstone for example.

“I just couldn’t keep up with Charles because he had much more front wing than I did and then I couldn't turn the car. It was the same today.”

Leclerc, meanwhile, was pleased with his personal performance on his way to second place – and believed that Ferrari would have had the same result regardless of whether they had tried a one-stop strategy like Mercedes.

“I mean it was a good race and I enjoyed the race,” he said. “I enjoyed the first lap with Max. I enjoyed later on, as well, with Lando [Norris] and Max again and that was nice. The pace was quite strong as well.

“Mercedes, though, saw something that maybe Red Bull and I didn't really consider seriously, which was the one-stop and they made it work very nicely. So, this is something we'll have to analyse but the whole race has been very good. And anyway, I think if we were on a one-stop, it wouldn't have changed much the results.”

In a similar vein to his team mate, the Monegasque was also hopeful that – with the upgrades added in Austin – Ferrari could be optimistic for the future and capitalise on the momentum they have built for themselves.

“I think so, but only time will tell,” he answered when asked if he felt they could continue this kind of run. “I think in the last three, four races we had upgrades on the car in a direction that I quite like, that we are pushing in, and it makes me feel a bit more confident with the car and so I'm optimistic for the future.

“Then it's also true that we are at the end of the season. We are not expecting to bring anything, any big upgrades. But now it's all about optimising what we have, and we are not in a bad place, so I'm looking forward to see how it will be like on different tracks in the next two weeks.”

title: When is the earliest Antonelli could win the title?
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has remained at the top of the drivers’ standings since Round 3 of the campaign in Japan – and his hold on the P1 slot was strengthened following his victory at the United States Grand Prix.

The Italian is now 123 points clear of closest challenger George Russell following the 18th event of the season, while third-placed Lewis Hamilton is now 124 points adrift.

Antonelli has previously insisted that thinking about the title is “exactly what I don’t want to do”, but following his win in Austin, even the Italian started to discuss how close he was to that maiden World Championship crown...

How many points are still up for grabs?

Five rounds remain in the 2026 season, with the next being the Mexico City Grand Prix.

This means that the maximum points score still available is 125, which would be achieved by a driver winning every remaining Grand Prix.

Drivers' standings after the United States GP

Which drivers are still in contention for the title?

Mathematically, two drivers besides Antonelli are still in contention for the championship – just Russell and Hamilton can beat the Italian now.

However, the realistic likelihood of either taking the title is slim, with their chance of winning based on the possibility of Antonelli failing to score any more points and one of the duo winning every race until the end of the season.

In this scenario, Russell or Hamilton could seal the title in Abu Dhabi.

When could Antonelli claim the World Championship?

Antonelli had a chance of winning the title at the United States Grand Prix, and he almost did it too. He needed to win the race and have Hamilton finish fifth or lower, and Russell finish ninth or lower.

While the 20-year-old held up his end of the bargain with victory in Austin, Hamilton finished fourth and Russell eighth to deny him the title.

But his maximum score means it is very likely that Antonelli will win the title in Mexico City. For this to happen, Antonelli would need to finish at least ninth. If he does so, it does not matter where Russell or Hamilton finish, the title will belong to the Italian.

In other words, Antonelli needs to score just two more points to take the title. If he fails to score, he will still take the title if neither Russell nor Hamilton win the race.

If Antonelli finishes P10, Russell can keep the title fight going to Sao Paulo with a victory.

When can Mercedes clinch the Teams' Championship?

Following their 29-point haul from Austin, Mercedes can seal the Constructors' Championship title in Mexico City, although it remains a long shot with Ferrari still very much in contention.

If they take a 1-2, then the Silver Arrows need Ferrari to score four points or fewer to take the title next weekend.

If Antonelli and Russell take the win and a third place, they need Ferrari to score one point or less.

Any other scenario sees that title battle move on to the next round in Sao Paulo.
